_doc: PRISM layout library — the grid FAMILIES (swiss/japanese/bauhaus/editorial) + the notable ARRANGEMENT patterns (column splits / archetypes) they legalise. A family is the constraint set that bounds how components may be placed on a slide; an arrangement is one legal row shape within one or more families. Ground truth: solver/grid-families.json (frozen params, each with a _src research ref), solver/families.py (freeze validation), solver/beam.py + solver/score.py (9 weighted scoring terms), docs/research/typographic-layout-systems.md (the design-system origins). This library is the human-/LLM-readable decision layer OVER those frozen params — it never invents a param, only names when each family/arrangement is the right one. Shared schema with the components + visualizers libraries: entries[] carry id/name/one_liner/when_to_use/avoid_when/info_depths/carries/density/pairs_with/source_ref.
selection_guide: Pick a FAMILY first (the mood + content character of the whole deck), then let the solver pick the ARRANGEMENT (row shape) from that family's split_whitelist by scoring the 9 terms. Family = constraint; arrangement = the specific legal placement. swiss when the content is analytical and dense and wants an objective modular grid; japanese when it is sparse and premium and the interval between elements should breathe (Ma); bauhaus when it is bold, high-contrast and one element must dominate kinetically; editorial when it is prose-forward, reading-paced, mixing text with a supporting visual. When unsure, swiss is the safe default (widest legal split set, mid density). The concrete number-and-type -> family+arrangement mappings live in layout_selection_guide below.

info_depth_legend.L1: glance — one claim, lowest density, most whitespace; board/executive first read
info_depth_legend.L2: scan — a small set of related claims, moderate density; the working middle depth
info_depth_legend.L3: read / expert — dense, many claims, highest legal fill; technical deep read

density_legend.airy: lowest density ceilings, largest deliberate void (japanese)
density_legend.dense: mid-high ceilings, modular grid fills its modules (swiss)
density_legend.kinetic-dense: highest ceilings, a full dynamic field with size/weight/direction contrast (bauhaus)

entries.name: Swiss / International Typographic Style
entries.one_liner: Objective modular grid — the neutral, analytical, evenly-organised default.
entries.when_to_use: Analytical and information-dense decks: metrics, comparisons, tables, structured evidence. Encodes Müller-Brockmann's modular grid + Gerstner's grid-as-programme + Ruder's active-but-restrained whitespace — the designer as neutral conduit, content organised logically over a proportional module system. Best when there is a lot to show and it must read as ordered, not dramatic. Widest legal split set (even peer sets allowed), so it is also the safe fallback family.
entries.avoid_when: The slide is a single statement that should breathe (use japanese) or one element must dominate the eye kinetically (use bauhaus). Its restraint (asymmetry_bias 0.4, dominance 1.5x) reads as flat when the content wants drama.
entries.source_ref: typographic-layout-systems.md §1 (Müller-Brockmann modular grid, Gerstner mobile grid, Ruder active whitespace); grid-families.json families.swiss (split_whitelist 12/6-6/8-4/4-8/4-4-4/3-3-3-3, restraint _src :53-54,:98,:108)

entries.name: Japanese spatial aesthetics (Ma / notan)
entries.one_liner: Sparse, breathing, asymmetric — the interval between elements IS the content.
entries.when_to_use: Sparse, premium, high-impact slides: one focal claim isolated by space, a single quote, an executive glance. Encodes Ma (負 negative space as fullness), notan (filled/empty mass balance) and asymmetric balance-by-relationship. Highest whitespace floor (0.3) and largest legal void (0.55), lowest density ceilings, strongest focal dominance (2.5x) because isolation-by-space reads as strength. Mandates at least one void/spacer cell.
entries.avoid_when: The content is genuinely dense (many peers, tables) — its low ceilings will refuse to fit them and either overflow or drop content. Also avoid for true symmetric peers: 6|6 is deliberately EXCLUDED (balance comes from relationship, not mirroring).
entries.source_ref: typographic-layout-systems.md §3 (Ma :145-147, notan :148-159, asymmetric balance :150-151,:160); grid-families.json families.japanese (6|6 EXCLUDED :150-151,:160; whitespace_floor 0.3; max_void 0.55; dominance 2.5x)

entries.name: Bauhaus / New Typography
entries.one_liner: Bold, high-contrast, kinetic — one element dominates, the field is dynamic.
entries.when_to_use: Bold, conceptual, attention-grabbing slides: a big number, a provocation, a title moment, a creative-audience opener. Encodes Tschichold/Bayer/Moholy-Nagy: reject symmetry, strikingly asymmetric composition, diagonal/kinetic scan, contrast of size/weight/direction. Highest dominance (3.0x) and highest asymmetry (0.9), loosest alignment (0.5) so a diagonal reading path is allowed, and the highest density ceilings for a full dynamic field.
entries.avoid_when: Calm, ordered, reference-grade content (use swiss) or airy premium reads (use japanese). Its 3x dominance + loose baseline will make a page of equal peers look chaotic — it needs a clear hero to justify the kinetic contrast.
entries.source_ref: typographic-layout-systems.md §2 (reject symmetry :121-122, diagonal/kinetic :124-135, size/weight contrast rule#10 :276); grid-families.json families.bauhaus (dominance 3.0x = MAX contrast; asymmetry 0.9; alignment 0.5; 6|6 only as z-quadrant :134,:347)

entries.name: Editorial grid theory (column / hierarchical)
entries.one_liner: Prose-forward magazine column grid — text flow with a supporting visual.
entries.when_to_use: Reading-paced, prose-heavy slides that still carry a visual or a stat rail: narratives, feature spreads, articles, a paragraph beside a chart. Encodes the editorial 5-grid taxonomy (column + hierarchical). Measure-driven 7|5 / 5|7 primary splits and a RAISED prose measure floor (6 cols, not 5) to protect the 45-75ch line-length ideal. Moderate dominance (2.0x) for hierarchical hero spreads; wide margins are the void budget.
entries.avoid_when: Pure data density with no prose (swiss packs it tighter) or a single sparse statement (japanese breathes better). Its prose_measure_floor of 6 means it will refuse to put body text in a narrow rail — good for reading, wrong for a metrics wall.
entries.source_ref: typographic-layout-systems.md §4 (5-grid taxonomy :171-188 manuscript/column/modular/baseline/hierarchical) + §5 measure 45-75ch :222-224; grid-families.json families.editorial (7|5/5|7 primary; prose_measure_floor 6)

entries.name: Manuscript / full-width stack
entries.one_liner: One full-width column per row — the conservative stack, no split.
entries.when_to_use: A single block, pure prose, or a lone statement/quote. The layout.py `None` case: emit no split, stack full-width bands. Universal — legal in every family (the [12] split). In japanese it becomes the airy Ma default; in editorial it is the manuscript grid for long prose.
entries.avoid_when: Two or more peer/heterogeneous blocks that would read better side-by-side — a stack wastes the horizontal axis and kills scanning contrast.
entries.source_ref: typographic-layout-systems.md §4 manuscript grid :173,:184; §8 stack(None); layout.py:28-30,:239 (1 block stays full-width)

entries.name: Duo (6|6) — two true peers
entries.one_liner: Even 6|6 split for two genuinely comparable blocks.
entries.when_to_use: Exactly two peer blocks of equal weight: a comparison, two options, a table beside a table. Symmetry must be EARNED (the blocks are actual peers), not a default. Legal in swiss, editorial, bauhaus. In bauhaus 6|6 is admitted only as the z-pattern 2x2 quadrant.
entries.avoid_when: The two blocks have unequal weight (use 8|4 hero+rail or 7|5 split instead) — an even split on unequal content reads as false symmetry. EXCLUDED in japanese entirely (balance-by-relationship, never mirroring).
entries.source_ref: typographic-layout-systems.md §2 rule 'symmetry earned not default' :132; §8 duo; layout.py:186-190 (duo two comparable-wide); grid-families.json japanese _src (6|6 excluded)

entries.name: Hero + rail (8|4 / 4|8)
entries.one_liner: Dominant artifact (8) leads a supporting detail rail (4) — asymmetric hierarchy.
entries.when_to_use: One dominant block (chart, simulator, big visual, key claim) with a short supporting text/callout rail. The workhorse hierarchical arrangement — 2:1 span ratio satisfies the 'hero >= 2x supporting' contrast rule. Legal in all four families; sidebar (4|8) is the mirror when the lead rail comes first (e.g. a checklist beside substantial main).
entries.avoid_when: Two true peers (use 6|6 duo) or a single block (use manuscript). If the rail content actually needs prose width, editorial's measure floor will reject a 4-col rail — promote it to 5|7.
entries.source_ref: typographic-layout-systems.md §1 Ruder contrast :108, §8 hero+rail; layout.py:155-159 (HERO block + short rail); rule#10 dominance :276

entries.name: Sidebar (4|8) — lead rail beside main
entries.one_liner: Narrow lead rail (4) then a substantial main block (8).
entries.when_to_use: A lead-in rail (checklist, index, small stat column) that precedes a substantial main body. The mirror of hero+rail with the rail FIRST in reading order. Legal in all families.
entries.avoid_when: The rail carries body prose (sub-45ch measure) — editorial forbids prose in a 4-col cell. Also avoid when both sides are peers (duo) or the main should dominate visually from the left (hero+rail).
entries.source_ref: typographic-layout-systems.md §8 sidebar (Hierarchical grid); layout.py:194-198 (lead rail beside substantial main)

entries.name: Split, mirrored (7|5 / 5|7)
entries.one_liner: Text<->visual 7|5, mirrored to 5|7 on the next split for rhythm.
entries.when_to_use: Text beside a visual where the text needs near-measure width (7 cols protects line length). Alternating 7|5 then 5|7 across consecutive rungs is rhythm-through-alternation (Ruder). Primary editorial split; also legal in japanese. This is the measure-safe alternative to hero+rail when the text side must not go narrow.
entries.avoid_when: swiss and bauhaus do NOT whitelist 7|5 — use 8|4 there instead. Avoid when content is a single block or true peers.
entries.source_ref: typographic-layout-systems.md §1 Ruder rhythm :110, §5 measure :222-224, §8 split; layout.py:200-214 (mirrored split); grid-families.json editorial/japanese whitelists

entries.name: Asymmetric lead (9|3 / 3|9)
entries.one_liner: Strong 3:1 split — a commanding lead block over a thin rail.
entries.when_to_use: Maximum in-row dominance: a focal block that must clearly command, with a thin supporting sliver. The most asymmetric legal two-cell split. Legal in japanese (focal isolated by space) and bauhaus (kinetic contrast) — the two high-dominance families. Reads as balance-by-relationship (japanese) or kinetic hierarchy (bauhaus).
entries.avoid_when: swiss and editorial do NOT whitelist 9|3 (too extreme for their restraint) — use 8|4 there. The 3-col rail cannot hold body prose (sub-measure). Avoid for peers.
entries.source_ref: typographic-layout-systems.md §2 kinetic contrast :124-126, §3 focal-by-space :145-147; grid-families.json japanese/bauhaus whitelists (9|3); dominance 2.5x/3.0x

entries.name: Triptych (4|4|4) — three peer modules
entries.one_liner: Three equal columns for three peer items — the balanced module row.
entries.when_to_use: Exactly three peer blocks of equal weight: three metrics, three options, three steps. The 12/3 even module split (Gerstner mobile-grid denominator). Legal in swiss and editorial. First rung of a modular field.
entries.avoid_when: Fewer than 3 or heterogeneous weights (use hero+rail or duo). japanese and bauhaus do NOT whitelist 4|4|4 (they favour dominance over equal thirds).
entries.source_ref: typographic-layout-systems.md §1 modular grid :56-67, §4 modular :175; §8 tiled grid; layout.py:102-121 (_tile 3->4|4|4); grid-families.json swiss/editorial whitelists

entries.name: Quad tile (3|3|3|3) — four peer modules
entries.one_liner: Four equal columns / a modular field row for four+ peers.
entries.when_to_use: Four peer blocks of equal weight, or the row unit of a true N×M modular grid (Brockmann modular grid, editorial 'modular' checkerboard for dashboards/catalogs). The 12/4 even split. swiss-only in the frozen whitelists — the most objective, most modular arrangement.
entries.avoid_when: Only swiss whitelists 3|3|3|3 — no other family. Cells this narrow (3 cols) cannot hold body prose. Avoid for heterogeneous weights or fewer than 4 peers.
entries.source_ref: typographic-layout-systems.md §1 modular field counts :48-49,:65, §4 modular grid :175,:186 (multi-row module); §8 modular-grid; layout.py:102-121 (_tile 4->3|3|3|3)

entries.name: Z-pattern (2x2)
entries.one_liner: Two 6|6 rows forming a 2x2 quadrant with a diagonal kinetic scan.
entries.when_to_use: Exactly four heterogeneous non-band blocks read along a Z scan path. The Bauhaus diagonal/kinetic arrangement codified — 6|6 is admitted in bauhaus ONLY as this z-quadrant. Two stacked duo rows scanned top-left -> top-right -> bottom-left -> bottom-right.
entries.avoid_when: Blocks that are actually peers wanting a flat modular read (use triptych/quad in swiss) or a single dominant hero (hero+rail). Needs exactly ~4 heterogeneous blocks to justify the diagonal.
entries.source_ref: typographic-layout-systems.md §2 diagonal/Z kinetic scan :134; §8 z-pattern; layout.py:257-258 (4 heterogeneous -> 2x2); grid-families.json bauhaus _src (6|6 as z-quadrant :347)

entries.name: Notan void — deliberate spacer cell
entries.one_liner: A content cell plus an intentionally EMPTY cell — void as structure.
entries.when_to_use: A dominant block deliberately paired with an empty spacer cell (e.g. 8 cols content + 4 cols void, or 9|3) so the interval itself carries the composition. Encodes Ma (interval is content), Ruder's active whitespace and Tschichold's structural white space. The void cell has no unit — it is a composition move, not under-fill. japanese mandates at least one such void/spacer cell (notan mass balance).
entries.avoid_when: Dense content that needs every column (swiss L3, bauhaus kinetic field) — an empty cell there reads as a dead hole, not active space. Only legal where the family tolerates a large void (japanese max_void 0.55). NOTE: aspirational — research rule #5 (spacer cell) is not yet a first-class layout.py archetype; today the scorer accounts void via whitespace/max_void, not an explicit spacer unit.
entries.source_ref: typographic-layout-systems.md §1 Ruder active whitespace :109,:255, §3 Ma/notan :145-159, §7 rule#5 active-whitespace/spacer :271 (marked new); grid-families.json japanese max_void 0.55 + 'mandate >=1 void/spacer cell'

entries.name: Band-lead — KPI bands first
entries.one_liner: Full-width KPI/metric bands promoted to the top, packed content below.
entries.when_to_use: Concept/board readers who want the headline numbers FIRST: promote KPI bands to full-width top rows (high-contrast headline ratio), then pack the supporting detail beneath. An audience-profile-driven macro arrangement, not a single split. Reads strongest in bauhaus (kinetic headline) and swiss (objective KPI grid).
entries.avoid_when: Expert/reading audiences who want the argument in flow (use editorial split) — leading with big numbers over-simplifies for a technical read. Needs genuine KPI/metric bands to promote; do not manufacture them.
entries.source_ref: typographic-layout-systems.md §5 headline ratio :239, §8 band-lead (Modular scale); layout.py:243-250 (band_lead profile promotes KPI bands + packed rest)

layout_selection_guide._doc: The rich components -> layout decision helper. Given the NUMBER and TYPES of components on ONE slide plus its info-depth, which FAMILY (mood/constraint) and ARRANGEMENT (row shape) fit best. Family is the deck-level mood choice; arrangement is what the solver's beam search then picks from that family's split_whitelist by scoring the 9 terms.
layout_selection_guide.how_to_read: 1) Read the deck mood -> family (analytical=swiss, sparse/premium=japanese, bold/high-contrast=bauhaus, prose-forward=editorial). 2) Read the slide's component signature (count + types) + info-depth -> arrangement. 3) Confirm the arrangement is legal in the chosen family (see each entry's `families`); if not, take the family's nearest legal split (e.g. swiss has no 7|5 -> use 8|4; japanese has no 6|6 -> use 8|4 or 9|3).

by_info_depth.L1: Glance. One focal claim. Prefer manuscript stack or a strong asymmetric lead. japanese (Ma) or bauhaus (big number). Lowest density, most void.
by_info_depth.L2: Scan. A small set of related claims. hero+rail, split-mirror, duo, triptych. swiss/editorial for order, japanese for calm. Moderate density.
by_info_depth.L3: Read/expert. Many claims, dense. triptych/quad-tile modular fields (swiss), split (editorial). Highest legal fill; avoid japanese (ceilings too low).

by_component_signature.why: A lone claim wants Ma — full-width, isolated by space. swiss/editorial manuscript also fine; japanese breathes best.
Headline number wants max contrast (dominance 3.0x). band-lead promotes it; asymmetric-lead 9|3 if a caption rides alongside.
Chart is the hero (8), statement the rail (4). swiss for analytical; japanese (8|4, focal isolated) or editorial 7|5 if the statement is prose needing measure width.
Prose needs 7 cols to hold 45-75ch measure; 7|5 protects it, mirror to 5|7 next rung for rhythm. NOT swiss (no 7|5).
Prose in the wide 7-col column; the two stats stack in the 5-col rail as small metric bands. editorial's raised measure floor keeps the prose readable.
Two true peers earn the even 6|6. swiss or editorial. If weights are actually unequal, drop to 8|4. Never japanese (6|6 excluded).
Three equal modules -> 4|4|4 (Gerstner 12/3 denominator). swiss/editorial only. Bold-audience variant: bauhaus band-lead with the three as KPI bands.
Four mixed blocks read along a diagonal Z (2x2). bauhaus kinetic scan. If the four are actually equal peers, use swiss quad-tile 3|3|3|3 instead.

5 does not divide 12 evenly; the modular fix is a mixed field: one 4|4|4 row + one 6|6 (or 8|4) row, not a single 5-way split. swiss modular grid across multiple rows. Consider promoting one card to a focal hero if weights differ.
A true N×M modular field (Brockmann/editorial modular): 6 -> two rows of 3 (via 4|4|4), 8/9 -> 3|3|3|3 rows. swiss owns 3|3|3|3. Dense, objective, checkerboard.
A short index/checklist rail (4) precedes the main body (8) in reading order. Any family; swiss/editorial for order. If the rail is prose, promote to 5|7 (editorial).
Manuscript grid: single wide column, generous margins, measure protected. editorial's home ground; swiss stack acceptable.

tie_breakers: Unequal weights -> asymmetric split (8|4, 9|3), never an even one (6|6, 4|4|4).
Body prose present -> minimum 5-6 col text cell (editorial floor 6); never prose in a 3-4 col rail.
Split not legal in the chosen family -> take that family's nearest legal split, do NOT switch family just to get a split (family is the mood decision).
When genuinely unsure -> swiss: widest legal split set, mid density, safe default.

family_chooser_status.encoded_today: solver/selection.py::select_family() is an explicitly-labelled DEFAULT PLACEHOLDER. It scores only two DECK-LEVEL signals — content_character in {analytical,narrative,conceptual,minimal,editorial} x audience_mood in {board,executive,technical,creative,reading} — via fixed CONTENT_BIAS + MOOD_BIAS affinity tables, deterministic, ties broken alphabetically, default swiss. It is documented as overridable: the solver merely CONSUMES whatever family name it is handed (SlidePlan.family); the real selector is W3/W5 pipeline territory.
family_chooser_status.aspirational_should_drive: The chooser SHOULD also read the PER-SLIDE component signature this guide encodes — the number and types of components + the info-depth (L1/L2/L3) — not just deck-level mood. Concretely: component COUNT + peer-vs-heterogeneous + prose-presence should steer BOTH the family and the arrangement (e.g. 6+ homogeneous peers -> swiss modular regardless of deck mood; a lone premium statement -> japanese; four heterogeneous blocks -> bauhaus z). Today's chooser cannot see component count at all, so it can pick a family whose split_whitelist does not fit the slide's real shape; the beam scorer then compensates within that family but cannot cross to a better-fitting family. The gap: promote family selection from a deck-level mood guess to a per-slide (mood x component-signature x info-depth) decision, using the by_component_signature mappings above as the encoded rule set.
family_chooser_status.note: This library entry is the human-/LLM-readable specification of that aspirational selector; selection.py is the runnable-but-minimal stand-in until W3/W5 wires the per-slide signal in.
